bullets.title: MU blowout Q3 re-rates memory sector; 16 SCAs signal structural shift
bullets.body: Micron reported F3Q revenue of $41.46B (vs. consensus $35.9B), EPS $25.11 (vs. $20.86), and gross margin of 84.9% (vs. 81.7%). F4Q guidance of $50B revenue and $31 EPS (both ~20% above Street) sent the stock +17-18% premarket. The headline news: 16 Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs) covering ~20% of DRAM and ~33% of NAND volume over 5-year take-or-pay terms, with $22B in cash deposits and $100B minimum cumulative revenue; management expects >50% of revenue under SCAs when complete. Supply tightness is now guided to persist beyond 2027, with gradual improvement only in 2028. Price targets cluster at $1,375–$1,675 across sell-side, with bulls modeling F27 EPS of $160–170.

bullets.title: AI capex trade reignited; Nasdaq futures +2.2%, Nikkei +4.6% on MU/QCOM
bullets.body: MU earnings and QCOM's Investor Day catalyzed a broad AI capex rally: Nasdaq 100 futures up 2.2%, S&P 500 futures +0.7%, Nikkei +4.6%, Korea KOSPI +5.4%. Memory ecosystem rallied in sympathy (SNDK +16%, WDC +12%, STX +10.6%). HF short-covering emerged in AI Winners (+1.4 std) and Mag 7 (+1.6 std) after Tuesday's record de-grossing, while retail ETF inflows tracking toward a potential $170B monthly record.

bullets.title: JPM raises SPX year-end target to 7,800 on ~10% consensus EPS upgrades
bullets.body: Dubravko at JPMorgan raised his YE26 S&P 500 PT from 7,600 to 7,800, citing FY26/FY27 consensus EPS upgrades of ~10% driven by the MU-led AI earnings revision cycle. JPM forecasts 2026 EPS of $350 (+29% YoY) and 2027 EPS of $390 (+15% YoY), maintaining a Tactically Bullish view.

bullets.title: QCOM Investor Day: non-handset revenue target doubled to $40B by FY29; data center $15B
bullets.body: Qualcomm raised its FY29 non-handset revenue target from $22B to $40B, with data center growing from ~$300M in FY26 to $5B in FY27 and $15B+ by FY29. META is confirmed as a CPU customer, MSFT as an accelerator sponsor. Near-term headwinds remain: Apple revenue rolling off by FY29 and handset demand softening on elevated memory costs. QCOM rallied ~10% premarket; Morgan Stanley upgraded to Equal-Weight ($231 PT) and JPM rates Neutral ($265 PT).

bullets.title: USD strength (~150bps move) creating dual headwind: tighter conditions + ~37bps EPS drag
bullets.body: 22V Research flags the current trade-weighted USD move of ~150bps has exceeded the 125bps historical threshold for meaningful equity impact. Each 1% appreciation subtracts ~25bps from EPS growth; the current move implies ~37bps of drag. USD is strengthening despite lower yields, signaling Fed credibility gains (Warsh perceived as more hawkish than expected), while gold has fallen ~25% since February as debasement premium unwinds.

bullets.title: Fed on hold; 22V sees 6/10 probability of 'easy' disinflation in H2 2026
bullets.body: The consensus view across several desks: Fed remains on hold through at least year-end (Piper's Kurt Lewis says into 2027). 22V Research assigns 6/10 conviction to an 'easy path' where core inflation slows to 3.3% YoY or below as fiscal stimulus fades — keeping markets biased higher. The hard path (Fed hikes to slow GDP, recession risk) is the tail. Hawkish Fed pricing (~33bps of hikes through year-end) remains an overhang.

bullets.title: ECB's Schnabel signals further rate hikes; JPM still forecasts September 2026 move
bullets.body: ECB board member Schnabel stated 'from today's perspective, we will need to raise interest rates further,' dismissing the Iran-US ceasefire energy price decline as insufficient to remove the tightening case. Core inflation is broadening into goods and services, keeping core above 2.5% YoY. JPMorgan continues to forecast one final ECB hike in September 2026.

bullets.title: Oil retreating to pre-conflict levels as Hormuz reopens; disinflation tailwind emerging
bullets.body: Brent crude fell below pre-conflict levels (~$72.48/barrel) as at least 20 tankers that had been stuck for 3+ months exited the Strait of Hormuz following the Iran-US ceasefire, with oil shipments running ~4.8M bpd. Lower oil is providing a disinflation impulse and easing rate pressure, a marginal positive for equities.

bullets.title: Bank stress tests benign: smallest CET1 drawdown in 7 years; WFC raises dividend 11%
bullets.body: The Fed's 2026 stress test showed the banking system's smallest CET1 drawdown in 7 years (1.6% vs. 1.8% last year) under the Severely Adverse Scenario, with the Stress Capital Buffer holding static at 2.5%. WFC raised its quarterly dividend ~11% to $0.50; USB raised 3.8% to $0.54. Morgan Stanley sees CFG, COF, and C as primary beneficiaries with buyback capacity above consensus.

bullets.title: Retail investor leverage showing tentative peak; prior peaks preceded multi-month corrections
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags retail options buying peaked June 5 at ~14M contracts — matching prior peaks in Oct 2025 and Nov 2021 that preceded multi-month tech corrections. NYSE margin (Net Debit balance) is at extreme historical levels with a tentative retreat. Risk parity leverage is also pulling back after hitting decade-plus highs in mid-May. Hedge fund gross/net exposure to US High Momentum remains at the 99th percentile despite 5% de-grossing since May 1.

bullets.title: AMZN AWS GPU pricing up 20% July 1; US e-commerce growth reaccelerating to 9.6% in 2026
bullets.body: Amazon is raising EC2 Block GPU pricing +20% effective July 1, a signal of continued AI infrastructure demand and pricing power. Separately, JPM's Anmuth sees US e-commerce growth reaccelerating to 9.6% YoY in 2026 (vs. 5.4% in 2025), with AMZN holding ~47% US share; the firm reiterates OW with a $330 PT.

bullets.title: EU designates AWS and Azure as DMA gatekeepers; 6-month compliance clock starts
bullets.body: The EU Commission reached a preliminary position that Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure should be designated as gatekeepers under the Digital Markets Act. Both companies have the right to defend themselves; if confirmed, a 6-month compliance deadline applies. This adds regulatory overhang to two of the largest cloud platforms.

bullets.title: Anthropic accuses Alibaba of large-scale Claude distillation via 25K fraudulent accounts
bullets.body: Anthropic alleges Alibaba used ~25,000 fraudulent accounts to generate 28.8 million exchanges with the Claude AI model between April and June 2026, calling it the biggest distillation attack on its systems by a Chinese company. BABA fell 4.4% to a 16-month low, compounding existing pressure from AI progress doubts and weak China consumption.

bullets.title: Global M&A on pace for $4T in 2026, best since 2021; IG bond issuance hits $175B record in June
bullets.body: Global M&A is tracking toward $4 trillion in 2026, which would be the strongest year since 2021. US investment-grade bond issuance hit a record $175B in June alone, fueled by AI-spending-related borrowing demand — a sign the capital markets backdrop remains supportive for deal-making and tech capex financing.

bullets.title: 2026 midterms unlikely to be a market overhang; Democrats favored in House, GOP holds Senate
bullets.body: Wolfe Research's midterm check-in concludes historical equity underperformance in midterm years is spurious (non-election-driven), and markets in 2026 have already outperformed the prior midterm-year average. Democrats are heavy favorites to win the House; Republicans are moderate favorites to keep the Senate. Both parties are running policy-light campaigns, and 2027 policy outcomes will be driven by debt ceiling necessity rather than campaign proposals.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples compressing: IGV -15.7% YTD vs. S&P +10.1%; AI moat erosion a growing thesis
bullets.body: Wolfe's SaaS index trades at 4.9x FY+2 EV/Sales (down 2.22% WoW), with security software at 7.3x and vertical SaaS at 5.2x. IGV has returned -15.7% YTD versus the S&P 500 at +10.1%, reflecting persistent concern that AI is compressing software moats — a thesis gaining traction as AI-centric software sees short-covering (+2 std) while broader SaaS shorts accumulate (-0.8 std).

bullets.title: KeyBanc card data: all-retail spending jumped +6.5% week of June 21, well above trend
bullets.body: KeyBanc's proprietary credit/debit card tracker showed all-retail spending accelerated sharply to +6.5% for the week of June 21, up from +1.5% the prior week and well above the 6-week average of +3.8%. June's run-rate (+6.5%) also compares favorably to May (+3.0%) and April (+4.0%), suggesting consumer spending re-accelerated into mid-June.

bullets.title: Power semiconductors forecast at ~82% CAGR through 2028 on AI data center grid demand
bullets.body: JPMorgan's international strategy notes AI data center power infrastructure (micro-grids, efficient power conversion) is driving power semiconductor demand at an estimated ~82% CAGR to 2028. Infineon is highlighted as the market leader with potential to capture ~€4B of a €14B power semiconductor TAM by 2028. This is a secondary AI capex beneficiary theme distinct from logic/memory.

bullets.title: India IT faces GenAI deflation headwind; JPM downgrades HCLT, WPRO to Underweight
bullets.body: JPMorgan downgrades HCL Technologies and Wipro (plus TATA Technologies) to Underweight, cutting P/E multiples 10–25% across the India IT board. The thesis: GenAI-led deflation and geopolitical uncertainty are keeping India IT revenue growth stuck at 2–3% for three consecutive years, with enterprise budgets crowded by AI token spending rather than traditional IT services.

bullets.title: Wolfe flags NVDA showing bearish lower-highs; rates cycle high may be in
bullets.body: Hedgeye/Wolfe signals: the 30-year yield signal has collapsed to cycle lows, yield curve compressed to +23bps, and Fed Chair Warsh expected to flip dovish in 3–6 months. NVDA is showing lower-highs with bearish trade/trend signals, described as 'the canary' for semis broadly — though the rest of the semi complex has not yet confirmed lower-highs.
